acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Marriage between parties was solemnized on 11.5.2012. No issue was born out of the wedlock. Appellant-husband challenged the judgment and decree dated 20.11.2018 passed by the trial court, whereby petition filed by respondent-wife under Section 11 read with Section 5(i) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 has been allowed.

legal_principles.principle: A marriage solemnized after the commencement of this Act shall be null and void if it contravenes any one of the conditions specified in clauses (i), (iv) and (v) of Section 5.
legal_principles.held: Section 11 of the Act provides that any marriage solemnized after the commencement of the Act, shall be null and void if it contravenes any of the conditions specified in Clause (i), (iv) and (v) of the Act.

legal_principles.principle: A person who contracts a subsequent marriage during the lifetime of a former husband or wife shall be punished with imprisonment and fine.
legal_principles.held: Section 494 of the Indian Penal Code provides that whoever, having a husband or wife living, marries in any case in which such marriage is void by reason of its taking place during the life of such husband or wife, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

outcome.final_order: Marriage between parties is declared as null and void by way of a decree of nullity.
